name: Mission
desc: The adversary learns what the mission is for, who depends on it and how it is built and operated.
defender: Know what you expose about the mission and which dependencies an outsider can map.

name: Exposure
desc: The adversary turns knowledge into capability: equipment, replicas, vulnerabilities, access and people.
defender: Reduce what can be researched offline and make weaknesses expensive to find.

name: Positioning
desc: The adversary obtains a first position in any segment from which the mission can be reached.
defender: Treat every segment boundary as an entry point, including vendors, terminals and the spectrum.

name: Control
desc: The adversary converts a foothold into the ability to execute: commands, code or privileged actions.
defender: Make command authority depend on cryptography and independent approval, not on network position.

name: Survival
desc: The adversary keeps access across resets, updates and investigations while avoiding notice.
defender: Assume telemetry and logs can lie; keep an independent way to establish the truth.

name: Transit
desc: The adversary moves between segments, spacecraft, tenants and organisations along trusted paths.
defender: Every trusted path is a route. Constrain what each path can carry and verify at both ends.

name: Manipulation
desc: The adversary collects, removes or changes data, parameters and signals without yet breaking the mission.
defender: Protect the integrity and provenance of what the mission produces and consumes.

name: Mission Effect
desc: The adversary denies, degrades, deceives or destroys the service the mission exists to deliver.
defender: Measure impact in mission terms and design so that a single effect does not end the mission.

name: Resilience
desc: The adversary attacks detection, response and recovery so the operator cannot return to a trusted state.
defender: Prove recovery works while under attack: rehearse it, time it and verify the result is trustworthy.
